title: Tidewater engagement — weeknote (integration progress)
summary: Weekly sync for Tidewater integration. Focus: private (VPC) deployment readiness, throughput regression from last load test, networking certificate/egress issues, and timeline for Dedicated reservation. Contains action items and owners.
content:
Meeting date: 2026-02-17
Attendees: Aisha Moreno (SE lead), Ravi Patel (ProServices PM), Elena Gutierrez (FieldEng), Connor Li (Infra SRE), Samira Khan (Customer eng rep - Tidewater), +Nina (customer infra)

Agenda:
- Quick status from Tidewater on environment prep
- Results from 02/15 perf run and root-cause triage
- Networking / cert issues blocking health checks
- Plan for canary rollout + Dedicated reservation timing
- Open risks and next steps

Notes / discussion highlights:
1) Customer environment / readiness
- Tidewater has completed VPC peering and provided subnet ranges. They still have a corporate TLS inspection box that rewrites certs for outbound connections; this is causing mTLS failures during healthcheck.
- Nina confirmed they will allowlist our control-plane IPs next sprint (ETA 2026-02-23) but need help validating ALB/NLB settings.
- Data residency: Tidewater requires audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance (S3 -> Kinesis). We confirmed Redwood private supports S3 bucket export; ProServices to provide sample lifecycle policy.

2) Perf regression from last load test (02/15)
- Test: steady-state synthetic workload (seq len 1024 typical, 25% spikes to 2048) against redwood-3b-int8 variant on a g5.2x pool.
- Observed: 95th latency increased from 220ms -> 460ms at target throughput (380 concurrent requests). Token/sec decreased by ~28%.
- Initial triage: KV cache memory pressure leads to frequent dealloc/realloc on long sequences; observed GPU memory fragmentation and occasional fallback to CPU kernel.
- Infra SRE (Connor) ran a kernel-level trace: small but frequent allocations at attention cache eviction path. Suspect model config mismatch (KV cache window configured for 512 by customer runner).
- Temporary mitigation: reduce max_sequence for canary to 1024 and use batching cap of 8 to keep latency inside SLO.

3) Networking / certificate issue
- Healthchecks from Redwood control-plane failing with 502 during ALB SSL negotiation due to TLS-inspection proxy presenting a different CN.
- Workaround: toggle healthcheck to plain HTTP port 8080 behind ALB for initial readiness; documented security caveat. Customer security team flagged as temporary-only.

4) Dedicated capacity & billing
- Tidewater is evaluating Dedicated (reserved pool) for predictable throughput. Need formal capacity estimate: initial request = 4 g5.2x-equivalent instances with burst to 6. Ask product for quota exception and commit pricing.
- Sales/Account lead pinged for contract draft. ProServices to provide a 4-week usage/lower-bound cost projection by 2026-02-21.

5) Rollout plan and runbook
- Canary step 1 (prewarm + low-traffic): deploy model variant with quantization q4->q3 fallback matrix; monitor latency, token error rate, and quality regressions with pre-defined prompts (see linked eval set).
- Canary step 2 (A/B 10%): route 10% of requests for 48h; if no regression, increase to 30% then full cutover.
- Rollback criteria: 95th latency > 2x baseline for more than 30m, or quality regression > 3% on eval set.

Quick notes / informal bits (scratchpad)
- Samira: "customer is nervous about falling back to hosted models due to PII flow" -> ensure fallback policy uses dedicated redacted path.
- Elena: add SRE playbook entry for kv-cache OOM patterns we saw.
- Aisha: need to create a short checklist for the customer with exact ALB/NLB config, security exceptions, and healthcheck curl examples.

Decisions captured:
- Use quantized variant (redwood-3b-q4) for initial canary to reduce GPU memory pressure.
- Healthcheck temporary set to HTTP 8080 until TLS inspection rule is updated (customer action).
- Reserve 4 g5.2x-equivalent Dedicated nodes pending pricing approval.

Open blockers:
- TLS inspection / cert rewrite: customer must allowlist control-plane IPs or provide bypass for healthchecks (owner: Tidewater infra, due: 2026-02-23).
- KV cache config mismatch: runner currently set to 512 window; requires config change to align with model weights or fallback to quantized variant (owner: Tidewater eng + Redwood SE, due: 2026-02-19).
- Contract draft / pricing approval needed before Dedicated reservation can be finalized (owner: Ravi / Sales, due: 2026-02-21).

Action items (owner - deliverable - due):
- Aisha Moreno - Draft ALB/NLB checklist, sample curl healthchecks, and runbook snippet - 2026-02-18
- Connor Li - Push microtrace for KV cache eviction and follow-up with runtime team (INF-2741) - 2026-02-19
- Elena Gutierrez - Add SRE playbook entry for kv-cache OOM pattern and quick mitigation steps - 2026-02-20
- Ravi Patel - Produce 4-week cost projection for 4 g5.2x equiv Dedicated pool + draft contract talking points - 2026-02-21
- Samira Khan / Nina - Confirm TLS-inspection bypass or allowlist and provide screenshot of ALB settings - 2026-02-23
- ProServices docs - share sample S3 -> Splunk export lifecycle policy and required IAM role step-by-step - 2026-02-19

Metrics snapshot from last run (02/15):
- Target concurrency: 380 requests
- Throughput observed: 820k tokens/hr (expected 1.14M tokens/hr)
- 95th latency: 460ms (baseline 220ms)
- GPU memory avg: 79% with spikes to 98% at sequence 2048
- Error rate: 0.8% (5xxs during ALB negotiation)

Questions for internal follow-up:
- Can runtime team simulate the exact allocation pattern we saw with KV cache window = 512? (Connor to escalate)
- Is there a recommended config change to the runner to avoid fragmentation for mixed sequence workloads?
- Product: can we offer a brief auto-tuning suggestion in Redwood Optimize for customers hitting this pattern?

Next sync: 2026-02-24 (same time). If TLS unblock happens earlier, plan a brief check-in to validate healthchecks and canary prewarm.

Raw notes / scratch (keep internal):
- Customer name: Tidewater (finance startup)
- Eval set: tidewater-sensitive-prompts-v3.json
- Observed one-off crash that matched a kernel panic on g5 driver (Connor logged to INF-2741)
- PR to automation repo to set canary prewarm flag: pr#12 (link in artifacts)
